data.description:
# A contributor can re-trigger an LLM-Review `-1` when it is infrastructure, not a finding

## Problem

An `LLM-Review -1` has two completely different meanings, and today a contributor can act on
neither:

* **A real finding** — `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` with inline comments. The correct response is
  to fix the code, amend and re-push.
* **A fail-closed coverage gap** — `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (…)]`. The review could not
  run, or ran and could not establish coverage. CONTRIBUTING.md §2c states this is "**not your
  code**" and that "a maintainer re-triggers it once infra recovers, don't 'fix' your diff".

So the documented remedy for the second case requires a MAINTAINER, because only the bots and
admins may vote `LLM-Review`. `recheck` re-runs CI (the `Verified` leg) and does nothing for the
review leg. A contributor whose change is blocked by an infrastructure hiccup is stuck waiting for
a human with elevated rights, on an otherwise-green change.

OBSERVED, which is what prompted this: Gerrit change 1189 took `Verified +1` (full CI green) and
`LLM-Review -1` tagged `coverage-gap (review-error)` — the review bot itself failed to run,
most likely a provider throttle while this session was running heavy concurrent LLM load. Nothing
was wrong with the diff, and no contributor-accessible action existed.

## What must be true — the safety property this ticket is really about

**A contributor must NOT be able to clear a real BLOCK finding by re-triggering.** That is the whole
risk. A re-trigger that a contributor can invoke on ANY `-1` would be a self-approval bypass of the
review gate, which is exactly what the two-label rule exists to prevent. So the eligibility decision
must be made by the BOT (or another privileged component), never by the contributor's assertion, and
must be derived from durable state rather than from the contributor's description of the vote.

## The discriminators that already exist — build on these rather than inventing a new one

- `review_bot/adapter.py` already classifies every non-PASS outcome and encodes it in the vote
  message via `_TAG_SUFFIXES[reason]`. The reasons are distinct and machine-readable:
  `finding` versus the coverage-gap family `gate-disabled` / `llm-unavailable` / `scanner` /
  `indeterminate` / `review-error`.
- `_coverage_gap_reason(coverage)` is the function that decides gap-vs-finding from the verdict's
  `coverage` block (`enabled is False` → gate-disabled; `llm_unavailable` → llm-unavailable; a
  fail-closed scanner abstain → scanner).
- **A stronger signal than the message text:** `review_bot/voter.py:277` notes that "a fail-closed
  review-error carries no verdict → nothing durable to persist". So a findings-based BLOCK persists a
  durable `code_review` artifact and a fail-closed one does not. Parsing a vote's message string is
  the weakest available discriminator; prefer durable state.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/` — the eligibility predicate and the trigger handling. This is where the
  gap-vs-finding classification already lives, so the predicate belongs beside it.
- the trigger surface a contributor uses (a magic Gerrit comment, in the spirit of `recheck`) and
  whatever listens for it.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2c and `docs/review-policy.md` — §2c currently instructs the contributor to wait
  for a maintainer; both must be updated, and `docs/review-policy.md` is described in §2c as the
  authoritative home for vote semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a contributor-invokable trigger re-runs the code review on the SAME patch set when the most
      recent `LLM-Review -1` on that patch set was a fail-closed coverage gap
- [ ] the trigger is REFUSED, with a message saying why, when the most recent `LLM-Review -1` was a
      real `BLOCK — finding`. Asserted by a test — this is the security property of the feature
- [ ] eligibility is decided by the privileged side from durable state, NOT from the contributor's
      claim and NOT from a contributor-supplied reason. A test asserts a contributor cannot obtain a
      re-review of a findings BLOCK by any input they control
- [ ] every coverage-gap sub-reason is covered explicitly and its eligibility stated:
      `llm-unavailable`, `review-error`, `indeterminate`, `scanner`, `gate-disabled`. Note these are
      NOT obviously all the same: an LLM outage is transient and re-running is right, whereas
      `gate-disabled` is a configuration state where re-running will produce the identical result
      forever. Decide each deliberately and record the reasoning
- [ ] a re-trigger that produces the SAME fail-closed outcome does not loop or spam: bound the
      retries or back off, and make the bound observable
- [ ] the re-review REPLACES the stale `-1` rather than leaving a contradictory vote history a
      reader has to reconcile
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2c and `docs/review-policy.md` are updated: §2c's "a maintainer re-triggers
      it" instruction becomes the contributor-accessible path, with the finding case still requiring
      a real fix
- [ ] no path is introduced by which a contributor can cause an `LLM-Review +1` to be cast without
      the review actually running and passing

## Explicitly out of scope

Changing the FAIL-CLOSED policy itself. A coverage gap must keep producing a blocking `-1`; that
behaviour was verified deliberately and is correct — a provider misconfiguration must never sail
through as a silent pass. This ticket makes the RECOVERY self-service, not the veto weaker.

## Notes

Filed unparented rather than under epic 061c: the epic is the LLM provider seam, and this is
review-workflow tooling. Re-parent if you would rather track it with the epic.
data.title: Contributor-triggerable re-review, allowed ONLY for a fail-closed LLM-Review -1 and never for a real BLOCK finding
